description: Apex OS vertical-slice architecture dependency boundaries. Consumed by scripts/architecture/validate-boundaries.mjs. Phase 0: enforcement covers only the new architecture roots; frontend/, backend/ and e2e/ are legacy-active and enter enforcement as their modules migrate.

legacyActiveRoots.reason: These are the live application roots serving production. They are excluded from enforcement until their modules migrate, per Phase 0 scope.

componentAliases.description: Short public aliases for migrated components, mirroring frontend/tsconfig.json paths. Declared here so the validator RESOLVES them instead of treating them as bare packages — otherwise an import reaching into a component's internals through its alias would be invisible to the rules below. Each alias must address a component root, never a file inside it.

apps.notes: Composition shells only. No business rules. One app must not import another app's internals.

platforms.notes: Cross-component and cross-platform imports must use a public index entry point.

shared.notes: Cross-cutting only. Importing a platform inverts the dependency graph.

database.notes: Bottom of the graph. Schema, migrations and the Prisma client import nothing internal.

rules.description: Frontend code must not import backend code.
rules.rationale: Server code must never reach the browser bundle.

rules.description: Backend code must not import frontend code.
rules.rationale: Server runtime must not depend on browser modules.

rules.description: shared/ must not import apps/ or platforms/.
rules.rationale: shared/ is depended upon by platforms; importing back creates a cycle.

rules.description: database/ must not import apps/, platforms/ or shared/.
rules.rationale: The Prisma client must be importable from every layer without a cycle.
Apps compose platforms, never the reverse.

rules.description: An app must not import another app's internal files.
Cross-component imports must target a component's public entry point, not its internal frontend/, backend/, shared/ or tests/ folders.
rules.rationale: A component's internals are private; only index.ts is public.

legacyFrontendImports.description: platforms/** importing frontend/** is FORBIDDEN by default. Migration phases may carry a narrow, temporary, per-component exemption listed below. Each entry names exactly one source component and an explicit allowlist of destination paths. platforms/** -> backend/** has no exemption mechanism and is always forbidden.

exceptions.reason: Phase 2A moved every Sales CRM dependency that is genuinely shared by two or more components. These four are not. leads.module.css is consumed by 15 Leads files and by exactly two controls; CompanyAutocomplete and CountryCodeSelect each have exactly one consumer (Leads), so moving them into the shared slice would create a 'shared' module that nothing shares. primitives.module.css IS shared by every Sales CRM component, but routing a CSS module through the shared slice's barrel changes its position in the bundle graph, and it is applied to the same elements as leads.module.css — a cascade-order change is a visual regression risk that Phase 2A explicitly declined to take.
removalConditions: CompanyAutocomplete and CountryCodeSelect move into the Leads slice, or gain a second Sales CRM consumer that justifies the shared slice
primitives.module.css moves once the remaining Sales CRM feature screens migrate, so all its consumers move together and cascade order can be verified in one step

exceptions.reason: salesCrmLeadsApi is a self-contained export, but it rides the module-local axios instance in frontend/lib/api.ts, which carries the Bearer-token request interceptor, the 401 redirect to /login?expired=true, the response.data unwrapping and a one-time nexus_*->apex_* localStorage migration shared by 58 files. Extracting the methods without that instance would either duplicate the interceptor chain (two 401 handlers, duplicated storage migration) or import it back from legacy anyway, reducing no debt.
removalConditions: The shared axios instance and its interceptors move to a platform- or shared-owned HTTP client
salesCrmLeadsApi is replaced by a Leads-owned API adapter built on that client

exceptions.reason: The Sales CRM auth adapter maps an Apex identity onto a CRM Role. It is the single point of contact between Sales CRM and the application-wide Zustand auth store, which is owned by the identity platform and must not move in a Sales CRM phase. Every other Sales CRM file consumes this adapter, never the store.
removalConditions: The application-wide auth store migrates to platforms/core/identity/
The adapter imports it through that component's public entry point

publicEntryPoints.notes: A cross-component import may address the component directory itself or its index file, but must not address a path inside it.
